attribution: Analyze recorded feedback against inputs, actual events and before/after artifacts. Return possible causes with evidence and uncertainty. Feedback is a claim, not proof; each feedback records its source (human, evaluator, reference, automated_check or downstream), so weigh it by where it comes from. Use only supplied artifact, event, Memory or feedback references. Do not invent a failure when none is supported. Set actionable to false when the feedback only thanks, approves or acknowledges the result and asks for no change; set it to true when it corrects the result, adds a constraint or preference, or reports a failure.
generation: Extract a reusable procedure from the recorded task history and the supplied attribution. The host explicitly requested generation after external confirmation; this is not independent validation. Cite supplied event, artifact, Memory or feedback references for every step and lesson. An artifact proves content, not that an action occurred. Do not treat feedback or a possible cause as proven fact. Keep case-specific names and answers in evidence only. Describe applicability, exclusions and checks. Keep the Recipe proportional to the task: a simple task needs at most 3 steps and no lessons. Every lesson must come from recorded feedback or an observed failure. Do not add steps or lessons about Memory screening, artifact persistence, feedback classification, evidence handling or other process meta-rules unless the recorded feedback explicitly asks for them.
acknowledged_only: The feedback only acknowledged the result; do not derive lessons from it.
improve: Update the supplied base_recipe using the new execution, feedback and attribution. Preserve unaffected valid steps and lessons; do not re-distill from scratch or require a separately selected cause.
